results.title: Legislation changes
results.description:
# Legislation changes
## Recent legislation changes
The Australian Government passes bills to update the [Fair Work Act 2009 (Fair Work Act)](https://www.legislation.gov.au/Series/C2009A00028) and related legislation.

New laws can have significant impacts across the workplace relations system. They can change rules and responsibilities for employers and employees.

Some changes affect the work we (the Fair Work Ombudsman) do.

Other changes can affect other agencies, including the [Fair Work Commission](https://www.fwc.gov.au/) (the Commission). The Commission is the national workplace relations tribunal and registered organisations regulator.

Find out more information about recent legislation changes below.

## Fairer Fuel
The [Fair Work Amendment (Fairer Fuel) Act 2026](https://www.legislation.gov.au/C2026A00020/asmade/text) received Royal Assent on 1 April 2026.

The amendment made changes to the Fair Work Act to help fast-track applications for road transport contractual chain orders.

Find out more on our [Fairer Fuel](https://www.fairwork.gov.au/about-us/workplace-laws/legislation-changes/fairer-fuel-reforms-to-road-transport-orders) page.

## Closing Loopholes
- the [Fair Work Legislation Amendment (Closing Loopholes) Act 2023](https://www.legislation.gov.au/C2023A00120/asmade/text), which received Royal Assent on 14 December 2023
- the [Fair Work Legislation Amendment (Closing Loopholes No. 2) Act 2024](https://www.legislation.gov.au/C2024A00002/asmade/text), which received Royal Assent on 26 February 2024.

The changes take effect at different times from 15 December 2023 to 2025.

## Protecting Worker Entitlements
The [Fair Work Legislation Amendment (Protecting Worker Entitlements) Act 2023](https://www.legislation.gov.au/C2023A00043/asmade/text) received Royal Assent on 30 June 2023, with changes taking effect at different times up to 1 January 2024.

These changes include:

## Secure Jobs, Better Pay
The [Fair Work Legislation Amendment (Secure Jobs, Better Pay) Act 2022](https://www.legislation.gov.au/C2022A00079/asmade/text) received Royal Assent on 6 December 2022, with changes taking effect at different times up to 6 December 2023.

These changes include:

## Paid Family and Domestic Violence Leave
The [Fair Work Amendment (Paid Family and Domestic Violence Leave) Act 2022](https://www.legislation.gov.au/C2022A00050/asmade/text) received Royal Assent on 9 November 2022, with changes taking effect at different times up to 9 June 2024.

These changes include an entitlement to 10 days of paid family and domestic violence leave which commenced for employees of:

- non-small business employers from 1 February 2023
- small business employers from 1 August 2023.

## Respect at Work
The [Sex Discrimination and Fair Work (Respect at Work) Amendment Act 2021](https://www.legislation.gov.au/C2021A00104/asmade/text) received Royal Assent on 10 September 2021, with changes taking effect on 11 September 2021.

These changes include:

## Previous legislation changes
We also have information about changes to the Fair Work Act and related laws that passed more than 5 years ago.

Find out more about [Previous legislation changes](https://www.fairwork.gov.au/about-us/workplace-laws/legislation-changes/previous-legislation-changes).

results.description:
# Guide to changing your plan
## Understand the ways a plan can change
### There are 2 ways we can change your plan:
- a plan variation (small change)
- a plan reassessment (significant change).

### What a plan variation is
A plan variation is a small change to part of your current plan. This might include small changes to:

- your goals
- your plan reassessment date
- the way you manage your funding
- provide funding for short-term supports if your situation changes suddenly
- add crisis or emergency funding because of a significant change in your support needs.

## Related information
### [What is a plan reassessment](https://www.ndis.gov.au/participants/changing-your-plan/types-plan-changes/what-plan-reassessment)

# Workplace Law Changes Employers Need to Know Before 1 July 2026
#### May 7, 2026
[Featured](https://www.hrstaffnstuff.com.au/blog/category/featured/), [HR Compliance](https://www.hrstaffnstuff.com.au/blog/category/hr-compliance-2/)

![](https://www.hrstaffnstuff.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/Business-owner-reviewing-workplace-law-changes-before-July-2026.jpg)

Deb

Update: the Fair Work Commission has now handed down its decision. Read our full breakdown of the [2026 award rate increases and Payday Super changes](https://www.hrstaffnstuff.com.au/blog/award-rate-increases-award-classification-changes-payday-super-what-employers-need-to-know-from-1-july-2026/).

## Workplace Law Changes Employers Need to Prepare for Before July 2026
There are a few changes on the horizon for the rest of 2026 that all employers need to be across.

## 1. Minimum Award Rates
As always, the Fair Work Commission (FWC) will apply an [award increase](https://www.fwc.gov.au/hearings-decisions/major-cases/annual-wage-reviews/annual-wage-review-2026/research-annual-wage) for all Modern Awards, effective 1 July 2026. The increase will be announced in June (usually in the second half of the month) and all employers should be ready to check their employees’ rates of pay against the new award rate entitlements.

Employers need to apply pay increases from the first pay cycle following 1 July.

## 3. Key Changes to Paid Parental Leave
From 1 July 2026, the Australian Government Paid Parental Leave (PPL) scheme will increase to a total of 26 weeks (130 days) for parents of children born or adopted after that date. This is the final stage of the scheme and adds two additional weeks to the entitlement.

The sharing of the PPL has also changed. For couples, the scheme sets aside four weeks for each parent. This means that more of your employees may choose to take longer periods of leave as these changes encourage the other (non-primary carer) parent to take up to four weeks of PPL.

All employers should update their Parental Leave policies to ensure they are compliant with the new rules.

## 4. Flexible Working Arrangements and Work From Home Laws
### Who Can Request Flexible Working Arrangements?
- are pregnant
- are 55 years of age or older
- are experiencing family and domestic violence, or
- are caring for or supporting an immediate family or household member who requires care or support because they are experiencing family and domestic violence

### Examples of Flexible Work Requests
- changes in hours of work (change to start/finish times, reduction in hours etc.)
- changes in patterns of work (split shift or job-sharing arrangements)
- changes in location of work (for example, work from home or an alternate location)

- if employees use their own computer, how can work product be protected?
